cover.dek: Breadth is green: 5 up 4% vs 0 down, 10-day ratio 2.75. Full size.

notes: Risk per trade: $50.00 (0.5% of $10,000.00; his band is 0.25-1%).
Position cap: $2,500.00 (25% of equity) in any one name.
Max 4 open positions (100% of equity if all are at the cap).

Day trades: FINRA deleted the pattern-day-trader count on 2026-06-04, but Fidelity has announced no migration date and may keep applying it per account until 2027-10-20, so run the account as if the old rule binds: at most 3 same-day round trips per rolling 5 business days in a margin account under $25,000.00; a same-day stop-out counts; a position held overnight never counts.

Account type: margin with debt protection (no borrowing, no good-faith violations). In a cash account buy only against settled cash (T+1); 3 good-faith violations in 12 months means 90 days of settled-cash-only.
Attach the protective stop the moment the buy fills, as a stop-MARKET order and never a stop-limit (Fidelity mobile: "Market + Stop Loss Protection"; Active Trader Pro: OTO/OTOCO).

reasons: down 4%: 0 < the scaled alarm of 3.2 (700 of 6,500)
up 50% in a month: 0 <= the scaled hot mark of 0.1 (20 of 6,500)

notes.text: a 10-day ratio below 2 is not an ideal time for swing longs
more than 0.1 names up 50% in a month is froth; a pullback usually follows
fewer than 0.9 names down 25% in a quarter is an oversold extreme; bounces follow in one to six weeks
T2108: under 20% is washed out, over 80% is stretched

plan.order_line: Buy 22 COIL stop-limit: stop $110.61 limit $111.72, day · OTO sell 22 COIL stop-loss $109.50 GTC
plan.order_readback: Buy 22 COIL stop limit 110.61 / 111.72 day, one-triggers-the-other sell 22 COIL stop loss 109.50 GTC
order_terms: A day order rests until the close unless you cancel it. The plan's entry is the first 30 minutes: if it has not filled by then, cancel it yourself; SpicyStock places and cancels nothing.
An open above the $111.72 limit does not fill at the open, but the resting order stays live and can fill on a pullback under $111.72 later in the day: cancel it rather than let it.
The sell stop at $109.50 is attached the moment the buy fills (OTO), as a stop-market order; nothing is protected before the fill.

exit_schedule.instruction: buy only if it trades through $110.61 (limit $111.72) in the first 30 minutes; the sell stop at $109.50 is live from the fill; cancel the day order yourself if it has not filled by the end of the first 30 minutes.
if same or next day, the price reaches $119.46 (+8% from $110.61): sell half and move the stop to 25-50 cents under that day's high.
at the close of day 1: the stop rises to the entry day's low if that is above $109.50.
if day 2 is green: do not move the stop to break-even before day 5 just because it is green.
at the day 3 close: sell at least half at the close. If day 3 closes at or below $110.61: exit: no follow-through.
raise the stop to each day's low (it never moves down); sell the rest into strength.
at the day 5 close: exit the remainder into strength.

watchlist.instruction: Buy only if it clears its trigger in the first 30 minutes on volume already above yesterday's pace; an open more than 2% above the close is gapped and needs a catalyst check before you buy.

_contract.schema_version: 2. The page refuses any other number rather than guessing at an older shape.
_contract.generated: When this file was written, ISO-8601 UTC. The page reads staleness off run.session, run.session_state and this, against the browser's clock in ET.
_contract.app: Who wrote the file: the app name, its version, and rules_version -- a 12-hex digest of the rules block, so two nights under different constants never read as one screener.
_contract.cover: The night's verdict as sentences: h1 (one of six fixed forms), dek, the primary action's label and anchor, and the verb. Composed from the numbers below; never edited by hand.
_contract.run: The run that produced this file: session, session_state, expected_session, status (ok|degraded|closed|failed), problems (stage, kind, message -- kind is one of seven words and the page prints one fixed sentence per kind), coverage, counts, email state, timings. run.sanitised counts the non-finite numbers replaced with null on the way in.
_contract.nights: The last twenty runs as a ring: session, status, published_at. The reliability dots.
_contract.account: The configured sizing assumptions every plan below was computed from: equity, risk per trade, the position cap, the slot count. Not a balance, not settled cash, not buying power.
_contract.rules: Every strategy constant, keyed by module. Archived so the record says which screener made it.
_contract.breadth: The Market Monitor for the session and the regime verdict with its reasons verbatim. The size multiplier is the regime's; the plans already carry it.
_contract.bursts: Every 4% or $ breakout the scan found, graded, with its plan when it has one, its summary sentence and its series (last 120 bars, trades and the closest miss only). Scored or refused, a burst is here; a name that never burst is not.
_contract.trades: Tickers of the bursts to trade tomorrow, ranked; those with order lines first. On a red regime this is empty whatever the grades say.
_contract.beyond_cap: Tickers of A-quality bursts with a plan and no ticket: withheld by the stop rule at the limit, past the slots or the configured equity, or sized to no whole share. Each has a reason in cash_budget.cut. Not checklist refusals.
_contract.cash_budget: Model allocation: what tomorrow's tickets would commit against the configured equity, the model slots used (open model plans count), and every plan without a ticket with its kind and reason. Never a balance or buying power.
_contract.watchlist: Anticipation names: top (with a plan each) and also_quiet, with counts. Alerts, not trades.
_contract.open_plans: Every published plan still inside its window, replayed to this session as a model: status word, the instruction sentence, and for an uncertain fill the reason. SpicyStock does not know what you hold: a plan you never took is a row to ignore.
_contract.scorecard: The rules' record over the published plans as a model of their fills, always with n, the read threshold and the uncertain count by reason. Rates are over settled plans alone. The rules' record, not yours. Null until a plan has settled.
_contract.closest_miss: On any night, the highest-scored burst not in trades and why it missed; the page shows it when trades is empty. Null when every burst is a trade or there were none.
_contract._contract: This paragraph per key. If a key is here and not above, or above and not here, the file is refused.
